title: 'Really bad!': Republican outrage mounts over Don Jr.'s billionaire-funded Bahamas blowout
text:
Kathleen Culliton is Raw Story's managing editor. She's been covering local and national news for more than a decade for outlets that include the New York Post, Al Jazeera, DNAinfo New York, Bustle, the New York Daily News, WNYC, NY1, City Limits and the New York City Patch. Kathleen is a proud alumna of the CUNY Graduate School of Journalism.

Yet another Republican lawmaker has condemned President Donald Trump's son for allowing a Russian oligarch to contribute a quarter of a million dollars to his Bahamas wedding blowout.

Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA) spoke out against Don Trump Jr. during an interview on "Face the Nation" Sunday morning.

"Anytime someone gives a $250,000 gift, and they have ties to the Kremlin, that's wrong," Cassidy said. "With that proximity to power, being the president's son, you've got to give faith to the American people that Washington is not a swamp."

Cassidy was responding to the bombshell ProPublica report on Trump Jr.'s lavish, three-day wedding party on a pair of exclusive private islands, which appears to have been "heavily funded" by Umar Kremlev, the International Boxing Association chief with close ties to President Vladimir Putin.

Democrats on the House Oversight Committee have since launched an investigation and even Trump has tried to backtrack, claiming his son paid the oligarch back.

On Sunday, Cassidy expressed relief on the latter point — but suggested he wasn't 100 percent convinced it was true.

"It would be nice to have that kind of verified," said Cassidy. "And no, it shouldn't have been done in the first place."

The Republican senator addressed Trump Jr. directly as he explained his logic.

"Even though in your mind it might be a gift," Cassidy said, "the appearance of it is really bad!"

Other Republican lawmakers who have heaped scorn on Trump Jr. include Sen. John Curtis (R-UT), who in a video address to his constituents, said he was outraged.

"It just stinks," Curtis said. "It's corruption, I don't like it.... this is a big deal."

Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) agreed, telling Washington Sun reporter Igor Bobic  he felt the gift was "beyond bad."

“Don Jr. is worth somewhere between 300 million and 400 million dollars," Tillis reportedly said. "Unless he has a cash flow problem, why on earth would you accept money from a Russian oligarch who's actually gone on delegation meetings with Xi Jinping in China?”
